title: Ambrosian Republic
capsule: The Golden Ambrosian Republic was a short-lived communal government established in Milan on 14 August 1447, the day Duke Filippo Maria Visconti died without male heirs, ending the Visconti line. Organized by jurists from the University of Pavia and civic elites, it was governed by twenty-four elected Captains and Defenders of Liberty (later reduced to twelve) and named after Milan's patron St. Ambrose. Though it repelled early Venetian and French incursions, chronic factional conflict between Guelph and Ghibelline factions paralysed decision-making, and the condottiere Francesco Sforza — initially hired to defend the republic — defected to Venice in 1448, then turned against Milan and reduced it by famine. A coup on 24 February 1450 opened the city gates; on 22 March 1450 Sforza proclaimed himself Duke of Milan.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The republic's territorial extent corresponds closely to the late Visconti duchy of Milan and is well evidenced through Italian communal records, though frontier fortresses changed hands repeatedly during the siege period.
